title: Stepwise engagement of cingulate ensembles underlies motivational decline in chronic pain
title_zh: 慢性疼痛中扣带皮层群体逐步激活导致动机衰退
abstract: Chronic pain can progress from sensory hypersensitivity to impaired motivation, but the underlying circuit mechanisms remain unclear. Using whole-brain activity-dependent tagging, projection-specific perturbations, in vivo Ca2+ imaging, and single-unit recordings in male mice, we identify stage-dependent engagement of anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) circuits during neuropathic pain. ACC neurons projecting to the basolateral amygdala (BLA) are preferentially engaged early, respond to allodynic stimulation, and contribute to mechanical hypersensitivity, whereas neurons projecting to the lateral habenula (LHb) are engaged later and contribute to impaired effortful persistence. Within the ACC→LHb pathway, complementary functional classes represent momentary response vigor and slower session progression, with persistence-related coding preferentially disrupted after nerve injury. Anteromedial thalamic input is biased toward ACC→BLA neurons, while recurrent ACC-BLA-ACC signaling provides a candidate route to later ACC→LHb dysfunction. These findings reveal a temporally organized cingulate circuit framework for the sensory and effort-related consequences of persistent pain.
abstract_zh: 慢性疼痛可从感觉过敏进展为动机受损，但其潜在的电路机制尚不清楚。我们在雄性小鼠中利用全脑活动依赖性标签、投射特异性扰动、体内钙离子成像和单细胞记录，识别了神经性疼痛期间前扣带皮层（ACC）电路的阶段性激活。ACC向基底外侧杏仁核（BLA）的投射神经元在早期更易被激活，响应所有痛觉刺激并参与机械过敏；而投射至侧髓核（LHb）的神经元则在后期被激活，并与努力持续性受损相关。在ACC→LHb通路中，互补的功能类别分别代表瞬时反应强度和较慢的会话进展，其中与持续性相关的编码在神经损伤后更易受损。前内侧丘脑输入偏向ACC→BLA神经元，而ACC-BLA-ACC的递归信号为后期ACC→LHb功能障碍提供了潜在路径。这些发现揭示了一个时间组织的扣带皮层电路框架，用以解释持续疼痛的感觉和努力相关后果。
